title: person-account-number — case shape (v0.2)
description: Pins protocol::account_number_from_person_id: the person account number is a display encoding of the LEADING 95 bits of the big-endian 16-byte person id, five bits at a time most-significant-first through the Crockford alphabet, plus the frozen Damm-32 check character over those 19 indices (account-number.md §3.1, protocol.md §3.1). Nothing else about the scheme moves: the MY- prefix, the alphabet, the 95-bit width, the check character, the 4-char grouping and the account_number_hash rule are the values account-number/v0.1 already pins, so one parser validates a person number and a generated one. `input_person_id_hex` is the NORMATIVE input (this family owns id to number); `input_phrase_utf8_hex` is carried on the cases that start from a phrase so a port can also pin the phrase-to-id hop. Reference implementation: protocol/src/account_number.rs (main myne repository).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'person-account-number/v0.2/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

oneOf.title: derive — person id in, canonical + display + hash out

input_phrase_utf8_hex.description: Informational: the normalized phrase whose SHA-256('myne.person-id|' || phrase)[:16] is input_person_id_hex. Present only on the cases that start from a phrase, so a port can pin the first hop too.

input_person_id_hex.description: 16-byte person id. The number takes the TOP 95 bits of its big-endian value (u128 >> 33), not the low 95.

expected_canonical_ascii.description: 19 Crockford entropy characters + 1 Damm-32 check character, uppercase.

expected_display_ascii.description: 27-character display form: MY- then five 4-character groups.

expected_account_number_hash_hex.description: SHA-256(canonical_ascii)[:16]. The same rule account-number/v0.1 pins for a generated number.
